verdicts.strongest_argument: The item codes defeat the finding. This 8-K carries item 7.01 - Regulation FD Disclosure - together with item 9.01, which means the company made a public disclosure and attached the document it disclosed. Regulation FD exists precisely to compel broad public dissemination; an issuer files under 7.01 when it has put information in front of the whole market, typically by press release. So the most likely state of the world is that Toro announced this on 2026-07-22 to everybody, and the reason it is absent from this corpus is that the capture ran no news search for this ticker (n_queries=0 in every admissible sweep) and stored a Stocktwits dump with two messages after 08-05. That is a capture artefact, not evidence the market did not see it, and I am instructed not to read it as a concession. I keep the score at the middle rather than higher only because the body is not stored, so I cannot confirm what was disclosed, and the finding is right that nothing in the corpus connects it to the print. Everything else about it is small: Toro is a 15.9% realised-vol industrial with a 3.02% median print reaction and a 1.51% deadband, and the tape shows no reaction whatsoever - run_up_20d +0.23% and the stock 2.56% off its 52-week high. The corroboration offered is a generic 'priced on margin expansion' analytic piece, which is true of most quality industrials and carries no size. The stated lean is 'slightly negative on the reaction base rate', which is a statement about history, not about this filing.
